content.title: Tyson Fury defeats Arslanbek Makhmudov; fight card results, highlights
content.text: Updated April 11, 2026, 5:21 p.m. CTFormer lineal heavyweight champion Tyson Fury is returning from retirement to face Arslanbek Makhmudov.Fury's return headlines a four-fight card from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on April 11.Tyson Fury scored his first win since 2023, returning from a nearly 16-month long retirement to defeat Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decision in a headlining bout from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.The judges scored the bout 120-108, 120-108 and 119-109.After the bout, in a scene straight from WWE, Fury grabbed the mic and stared down fellow British boxing superstar Anthony Joshua, who was ringside, and promptly called him out for a bout later this year. Saudi Arabian powerbroker Turki Alalshikh has long teased a blockbuster clash between the pair and was in the ring afterwards to fuel the fire."Next, I want to give you the fight you've all been waiting for," Fury said in the ring. "I want you, AJ, Anthony Joshua. Let's give the fight fans what they want, the battle of Britain. And here's my challenge, I challenge you, Anthony Joshua, to fight me, 'The Gypsy King,' next. Do you accept my challenge?"Joshua was handed the mic ringside and indicated he too wants the bout, but wouldn't confirm that it will come next, pointing to previous contract negotiations with Fury which turned sour."Tyson, I've never had no problem getting in the ring with you," Joshua said. "I punched you out when we were kids and after watching you tonight, I'll punch you up again ... you know I'll sit across that ring from you in due time."You ain't going to tell me what to do. I've been chasing you for the last 10 years. When you're ready, you come and see me and tell me your terms and conditions and I'll have you in the ring when I'm ready. I'm the boss."In order to secure a potential Joshua bout, Fury had to successfully come back against Makhmudov. That proved little trouble for the former lineal champion, who lost only one round across all three judges' scorecards.See below for The Tennessean's live updates throughout the Fury vs. Makhmudov fight card. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov fight card resultsTyson Fury def. Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decisionConor Benn def. Regis Prograis by unanimous decisionRichard Riakporhe def. Jeamie Tshikeva by TKO in Round 5Justis Huni def. Frazer Clarke by majority decision Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 12Into the final round and Makhmudov no doubt needs a knockout to have his hand raised at this stage. Fury landing a few early hooks as the pair tie up in the center. Again on the inside Fury connects with a right uppercut, before soon after backing Makhmudov against the ropes and landing a clean hook. Fury digging to the body on the inside and picking Makhmudov apart from range, raising his hands as the final bell sounds. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 11It gets messy along the ropes early, as each fighter looks for an opening to connect at close range. Fury continues to connect with the jab, but hasn't been able to build upon it with Makhmudov continually clinching. Midway through the round Fury begins to find some more openings in between clinches, picking out some solid shots to the body before following to the head. Fury clocks Makhmudov with a left hook in the corner before the bell, capping off another strong round. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 10Fury continues to chop away at Makhmudov and just past the one-minute mark knocks his mouthpiece loose. As Fury presses forward it's forced numerous clinches, slowing the pace of this round. Fury turns and locks Makhmudov along the ropes, landing a handful of shots before being pushed to the canvas illegally. Just before the bell Fury clocks Makhmudov with a pair of clean hooks. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 9Fury outlanding Makhmudov 106-44 at the start of the round. Plenty of clinching early on, giving Fury a chance to chop away with short body shots. Fury continues to pump the jab before jumping inside and landing to the body. Makhmudov lands a right hand now as he steps into range, but isn't able to follow up. Fury closes the round with a few strong body shots just ahead of the bell. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 8Makhmudov presses early and lands a glancing right hand before Fury slips out of danger. Fury comfortable with everything coming his way in this fight. Fury paws with the jab before landing another uppercut with the right midway through the round. Fury lands a strong left hook in the corner now and Makhmudov looks momentarily shaken. Fury shifts southpaw and applies the pressure with 30 seconds to go, but Makhmudov closed the round without taking further damage. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 7Fury lands a pinpoint jab early in the round before Makhmudov once again flies forward and forces a clinch. Fury lands a right uppercut as they trade at close range in the center, but moments later Makhmudov comes back with a right of his own. While clinched, Fury has been picking out short shots to the body of Makhmudov, while little has come back Fury's way. Fury didn't need much more than his jab that round. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 6Fury a step too quick for Makhmudov, having little trouble evading his pressure. Fury continues to pick out straight shots from range, with Makhmudov doing little to avoid them. Now Fury smiles for a moment as Makhmudov leans on him in the corner. Fury pops Makhmudov with two more crisp jabs as we head into the final seconds of the round. One way traffic midway through the fight. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 5Makhmudov lands an early left but Fury then keeps him at bay by continually pumping the jab. Now Fury pops Makhmudov with a couple solid jabs from range. Midway through the round and Makhmudov is yet to show a plan B, flying forward behind wild combinations which have done little to threaten Fury. Fury looking comfortable working from the back foot thus far. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 4Makhmudov glanced an early left hand off Fury, backing him up, but that's seemingly the extent of the damage. Makhmudov soon after crashes forward and forces a clinch with Fury, where they each connect some short, chopping shots. Fury lands a right hand and makes Makhmudov miss, following with another right before the two tie up. It's still messy in there, but Fury beginning to gain his rhythm. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 3Fury putting together some straight shots early, keeping Makhmudov at range. Fury continues to flash the jab from the outside, doing just enough to slow the flurries from Makhmudov. Fury has been able to stack a few body shots each time Makhmudov ties up with him, which has been plenty. Inside the final minute now, Fury has Makhmudov on the back foot as he lets the straight right loose, connecting to the head of Makhmudov. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 2Makhmudov pressing forward time after time, landing some glancing punches early as Fury moves around the outside to evade pressure. Fury lands a quick right hand from the back foot before Makhmudov crashes into him and clinches. Been a real sloppy fight, with continual clinches as Makhmudov presses forward into Fury. Fury looking better on the counter this round, but still not much landing for either fighter. Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov: Round 1We're underway as Fury ends his brief retirement from the ring, seeking further heavyweight glory. Makhmudov holding the center of the ring early as Fury works from the outside. Makhmudov is barreling forward with combinations, but Fury's handling the pressure with ease, tying up each time. Fury and Makhmudov each able to land a couple glancing shots, but overall it was a quiet round from both fighters in terms of connects. Fury vs Makhmudov undercard live updates Conor Benn scores unanimous decision over Regis PrograisConor Benn continued his winning ways in the co-main event, as he took down former world champion Regis Prograis by unanimous decision. All three judges scored the 10-round bout 98-92.Fighting at a 150-pound catchweight, Benn showcased his signature speed and although he wasn't able to score the stoppage against the rugged Prograis, there was little doubt about the victor at the sound of the final bell. Prograis competed well in the opening half of the bout, countering effectively from the back foot, but as the fight progressed Benn's output and intensity became too much for the 37-year-old former champ.Benn improves to 25-1 with the win, while Prograis falls to 30-4.See round-by-round updates from the fight below.Round 10: We're into the final round and barring a knockout from Prograis, Benn should take it, having seemingly built a comfortable lead. Benn a step faster at this stage, applying the pressure and changing angles on Prograis. Prograis having his moments, landing down to the body, but it's not enough to phase Benn. Benn continues to press forward in the final seconds, landing the left with relative ease ahead of the final bell.Round 9: Benn stacks some early connects as Prograis shakes his head, as if to say they didn't hurt him. Benn working more from range this round, making it hard for Prograis to get inside. The jab continues to land for Benn and he's following it up with some more good work to the body of Prograis. Prograis lands a solid left hand on the inside with 15 seconds to go, but Benn responds right back by cracking him on the chin.Round 8: Prograis having a tougher time responding with enough to keep Benn off of him. Benn continues to press forward, landing the jab through the guard of Prograis and continually digging down low. The output of Benn has been too much for Prograis this round. Down the stretch Prograis is catching many of Benn's shots on the gloves, but is still being pushed back by his power. Another good round from Benn.Round 7: Benn comes out of the gate whipping some looping shots and landing, but inside thirty seconds Prograis responds with a solid left hand. Benn working to the body of Prograis now and connecting some solid punches. Prograis looks to be losing steam, as Benn knocks him slightly off balance with a right hand, stacking real strong connects here. The body shots continue to connect for Benn. Inside the final thirty seconds now, and Benn closes the round with a handful of connects down low on Prograis.Round 6: The pair exchange early and Prograis lands a nice left hand. Benn probing from range now and lets a right uppercut loose, connecting to the body of Prograis before shortly after landing another uppercut to the head. A second cut has seemingly opened up above Benn's other eye now, leaking a good amount of blood. Now Benn's slipping in and out of range and landing some solid shots, while Prograis has been unable to hurt him down the stretch.Round 5: It's an aggressive start from Benn, who lands a few solid straight shots from the front foot. There have been plenty of tactical exchanges this fight, with each fighter taking and giving shots at close range. This round it's seemingly been Benn edging out the exchanges. Now Prograis urges Benn toward him before pounding Benn with a few strong lefts to the body. Benn lands some good punches down the stretch, but took his fair share from Prograis too.Round 4: Prograis continues to hold his ground in the center of the ring and has stacked a few early connects in the fourth. Benn digs down to the body but Prograis pushes back now, bringing the fight to Benn momentarily. Benn bleeding above his right eye now it seems. Benn landing some straight shots down the stretch but Prograis has taken them in stride and responded well on the counter. Best round so far for Prograis.Round 3: Benn letting his hands loose early, but majority of the punches are finding Prograis' guard. Benn continues to keep the pace up, but Prograis has remained in the pocket with Benn yet to land too many clean shots midway through the round. Prograis eating some jabs now to remain in range and counter, but hasn't landed anything to keep Benn off him. Benn looks in control, but far from dominant.Round 2: Benn continues to apply the pressure, shooting in and out of range and letting quick combinations loose, yet to land a significant shot this round though. Prograis now momentarily falls to the canvas after throwing a punch, but again it's a slip. Neither fighter doing much to separate themselves, each picking out one to two shots this round before moving back into space.Round 1: We're underway as Benn looks to follow up last year's win over Chris Eubank Jr., facing the former world champion Prograis. They both come out of the gate throwing plenty of shots, but nothing landing clean for either fighter in the opening seconds. Benn remaining active and steps inside to land a solid right hand to the head of Prograis, but it's not too long after Prograis connects with a one-two. So far Prograis letting Benn walk into range before trying to counter. In the final minute Benn momentarily drops to the canvas but it looks to be a slip. Then Benn lands a big right hand just as the bell rings. Richard Riakporhe stops Jeamie Tshikeva in Round 5Richard Riakporhe improved to 3-0 in his heavyweight campaign as he stopped Jeamie Tshikeva in the fifth round of their Bristish heavyweight title contest. Riakporhe has now scored three stoppage victories since making the move from cruiserweight to heavyweight in 2025.Riakporhe was dominant from the opening bell, picking the twice-beaten Tshikeva apart with a strong jab and thumping right hands throughout. In the fifth, Riakporhe landed a right hand over the top which sent Tshikeva down to the canvas. He'd beat the count, but it wasn't long before Riakporhe's subsequent onslaught forced the referee to step in and call a halt to the fight.Riakporhe is now 20-1 with 16 wins by knockout.See round-by-round updates from the fight below.Round 5: Tshikeva lands a few early jabs, pushing Riakporhe onto the back foot. It's not long after though that Riakporhe lands a thumping right to his head and drops him to the canvas! Tshikeva beats the count but looks hurt. Riakporhe hunting now, pounding away along the ropes, but Tshikeva shows good defense to avoid the shots. Tshikeva now gets thrown to the canvas by Riakporhe. Once up, Riakporhe continues the onslaught and as he lets his hands loose along the ropes the referee steps in and stops the fight! Perhaps a slightly early stoppage but a knockout seemed imminent.Round 4: Tshikeva active in the opening moments of the round, pumping the jab but not able to land any shots of real significance. Now Tshikeva has a point taken from the referee, seemingly for leading with his head. Another hurdle for Tshikeva to face now. Tshikeva lands a right hand over the top now but a clinch means he's unable to follow up. Riakporhe far less active this round, but inside the final minute he turns up the pressure and lands a couple big right hands.Round 3: Riakporhe using his reach well, continuing to land the jab early. Riakporhe lands a solid right hand now forcing a clinch from Tshikeva, moving forward without much fear of what's coming back. Tshikeva's been able to land the occasional hook to Riakporhe's body, but is never able to follow up and stack connects. He is doing his fair share of clinching though. It's been steady work from Riakporhe thus far.Round 2: It's just round two but Tshikeva is already looking uncomfortable in there against the taller Riakporhe. Riakporhe continues to find success with the right hand early and Tshikeva has begun to bleed from his nose. Riakporhe sticking his jab right through the guard of Tshikeva, landing consistently. Just before the bell, Riakporhe rolls with a left hand from Tshikeva, but it still connects on the temple.Round 1: Our second heavyweight contest is underway and Riakporhe takes control of the center of the ring as each fighter paws back and forth with the jab. Now Riakporhe lands a strong left hand followed by an uppercut, before the two tie up and fall over onto the canvas. Riakporhe rips another right uppercut and connects to Tshikeva's body. Inside the final minute, Riakporhe begins to back up Tshikeva after a pair of right hands, and just before the bell cracks Tshikeva with another right. Justis Huni edges out decision over Frazer ClarkeJustis Huni bounced back from his lone career defeat last summer, opening the main card with a majority decision victory over Frazer Clarke. One judge scored the bout 95-95, while the other two scored 96-94 in favor of Huni.It was an exciting heavyweight affair, one in which Huni outlanded and outhrew Clarke, showcasing superior footwork and hand speed as he changed angles and let combinations loose. Clarke had his moments throughout, thumping Huni with a handful of solid power punches, but ultimately Huni's steady pace and accuracy edged him the decision.Huni improves to 13-1, while Clarke falls to 9-3-1.See round-by-round updates from the fight below.Round 10: We begin the final round and Huni has seemingly established a slight lead, but it could feasibly go either way still. Huni working from the back foot and landing some solid left hands as Clarke presses forward and backs him into the ropes. Clarke teeing off against Huni along the ropes now but Huni moves well to avoid and take the sting off his shots. Huni continues to land to the body down the stretch, closing out another solid round which should see him take the decision.Round 9: They open the round with a back-and-forth exchange, Huni landing to the body while Clarke glances a few punches off his head. Huni looking more energetic at this stage of the fight, outthrowing and outmoving Clarke. Now Huni lands a solid right hand but Clarke continues to press forward and not long after lands a couple thumping shots on Huni. Both fighters land left hands down the stretch, as we close out the penultimate round.Round 8: It's a competitive start to the round as they go back and forth landing glancing shots. Now as Clarke applies the pressure, Huni cracks him with a pair of right hands before changing angles and landing the uppercut with the right. Huni digging to the body well but taking some shots in return from Clarke as they fight at close range. Down the stretch Huni lands an uppercut and successfully follows up with a second connect, but Clarke takes the shots well.Round 7: Clarke firing some big right hands early but hasn't been able to connect cleanly. There's a brief pause now as Huni loses his mouthpiece. We're back and coming out of a clinch Huni is able to connect a couple solid right hands, but it's not long after that he gets tagged with a strong body shot from Clarke. Into the final minute now, Clarke has been the aggressor but neither fighter able to land anything significant down the stretch.Round 6: Both fighters doing some good work going back and forth with the jab in the opening minute of the round. Huni continues to rip the left hook to Clarke's body with success. Clarke plodding forward but Huni's footwork has kept him out of danger as he picks out shots. Clarke lands a solid right and backs Huni into the corner late, but Huni comes back with a pair of right hands just before the bell.Round 5: Clarke opens with a few solid right hands at they clash at close range to start the round. Huni has his back against the ropes now and is able to fire off and land a couple straight shots with the right. Clarke now pops Huni's head back with a left hand inside the final minute, but Huni follows up with a handful of connects to Clarke's body. Tightly contested exchanges that round, with Huni still looking the quicker fighter.Round 4: Clarke trying to work his way inside behind the jab but he's getting caught with looping shots from the quicker Huni once within range. Now Clarke lands a solid right hand along the ropes, but Huni takes it in stride and moments later lands a flurry to Clarke's body. At close range in the center Huni lands a right before getting his head popped back by a Clarke uppercut. Huni comes right back though, connecting with a quick combination. Clarke tees off on Huni in the corner to end the round, but isn't able to land many damaging punches.Round 3: Clarke lands a solid right hand to Huni's head as the pair exchange in the center of the ring early. As Clarke ties up in the center Huni is able to land a couple solid uppercuts, neither fighter able to gain much momentum in the round thus far. Now Clarke lands a two-punch combination but as we head into the final minute Huni is beginning to stack connects. Both fighters are landing but Huni's been quicker to the punch.Round 2: Huni connects on a few early jabs as the fighters quickly get going in the second. Huni looking real sharp thus far, showing his speed as he peppers Clarke with left hands. Clarke continues to get tagged coming in, with Huni consistently hooking down to the body before following up to the head. Clarke's exchanging but generally he's only been able to land a single shot at time, getting beat to the punch by Huni.Round 1: We're underway and Clarke is flashing a sharp jab in the opening seconds. Now in the center of the ring Clarke lands a right hand before Huni counters with a quick flurry, connecting a couple glancing shots. Huni doing some solid work to the body. Inside the final minute now, punches fly back and forth and Clarke lands a thumping left to Huni's chin, but it's taken well. Huni closes the round with a pair of strong left hands, one connecting to the body and the other to Clarke's head.What time is the Tyson Fury fight today?Coverage of the Fury vs. Makhmudov headlined fight card will begin on Netflix at 1 p.m. (CT) on April 11. Ring walks for the main event are expected at approximately 4 p.m. (CT).Fight card start: 1 p.m. CTFury vs. Makhmudov ring walks: approx. 4 p.m. CTHow to watch Tyson Fury fight?Tyson Fury's comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov and the accompanying undercard will air live on Netflix, at no extra cost to subscribers.How to watch: NetflixFury vs Makhmudov fight cardThe undercard to Fury vs. Makhmudov sees the return of fellow British star Conor Benn, fresh off a unanimous decision victory over Chris Eubank Jr. in the same venue last November.Tyson Fury (34-2-1, 24 KOs) vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov (21-2, 19 KOs)Conor Benn (24-1, 14 KOs) vs. Regis Prograis (30-3, 24 KOs)Richard Riakporhe (19-1, 15 KOs) vs. Jeamie Tshikeva (9-2, 5 KOs)Frazer Clarke (9-2-1, 7 KOs) vs. Justis Huni (12-1, 7 KOs)Tyson Fury vs Makhmudov weigh-in resultsTyson Fury, 267.9 pounds; Arslanbek Makhmudov, 264.9 poundsConor Benn, 149.5 pounds; Regis Prograis, 148.1 poundsJeamie Tshikeva, 262.7 pounds; Richard Riakporhe, 234.12 poundsFrazer Clarke, 259.12 pounds; Justis Huni, 246.14 poundsTyson Fury fight predictionWhile Makhmudov poses a threat for any heavyweight, standing at 6-foot-5½ with bona fide punching power, there was a reason he was chosen as the opponent for Fury's comeback. Makhmudov is a plodding puncher, without the footwork or speed to outbox many of the division's top fighters.Fury's layoff could be viewed as a negative, but it's given him more than enough time to get into fighting shape, and a fit Tyson Fury should dance around Makhmudov, thumping him with power punches as Agit Kabayel once did on his way to a TKO victory.Makhmudov has still shown himself to be durable in the past, despite his two stoppage defeats, and at 37 years old it remains to be seen just how much thunder Fury has left in the gloves, but he should have little trouble pounding his way to a decision on the cards.Prediction: Fury def. Makhmudov by unanimous decisionTyson Fury vs Makhmudov oddsFury is a -600 favorite to emerge victorious in his comeback fight, while Makhmudov is a +400 underdog. The over/under is set at 8.5 rounds.Fury by KO/TKO: -165Fury by decision: +260Makhmudov by KO/TKO: +600Makhmudov by decision: +1400Odds via DraftKings, as of April 10Tyson Fury vs Makhmudov fight locationThe Tyson Fury vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov fight card will be held at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Fury previously fought Derek Chisora in the same venue in 2022, while it more recently hosted the first and second bouts between Conor Benn and Chris Eubank Jr.Location: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, UKTyson Fury recordTyson Fury is 34-2-1 with 24 wins by knockout.Fury reigned as lineal heavyweight champion for nearly a decade before suffering consecutive defeats to Usyk, first in a battle for the undisputed title. He'd previously held the WBC belt for four years, successfully defending three times while also defeating Francis Ngannou in a non-title bout.As he's returning from retirement, Fury is unranked at heavyweight.How old is Tyson Fury?Tyson Fury is 37 years old and stands at 6-foot-9 with an 85-inch reach. Fury has spent his entire career at heavyweight, weighting in at an average of 273.5 pounds across his last three bouts.Arslanbek Makhmudov recordArslanbek Makhmudov is 21-2 with 19 wins by knockout.Makhmudov is riding a two-fight win streak, most recently defeating British journeyman David Allen by unanimous decision last October. His two career defeats came in a three-fight span between 2023 and 2024, as he was stopped by both Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello.Makhmudov is a top 15 ranked contender with the WBA.Arslanbek Makhmudov weightArslanbek Makhmudov is 36 years old and stands at 6-foot-5½ with a 72-inch reach. Makhmudov is a career heavyweight and has weighed in at an average of just over 262 pounds across his last three bouts.Tyson Fury net worthWhile Fury's exact net worth is unknown, his two fights against Oleksandr Usyk in 2024 left him as one of the highest paid athletes in the world. Fury landed No. 3 on Forbes' May 2025 list of the highest paid athletes in the world, having reportedly collected $146 million the year prior.Sportico also ranked Fury No. 3 in its list of the highest paid athletes in 2024, trailing only Cristiano Ronaldo and Steph Curry.Boxing fights todayJuan Francisco Estrada vs. Tenshin Nasukawa; 3:30 a.m. CT, April 11; DAZNTyson Fury vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov; 1 p.m. CT, April 11; NetflixVito Mielnicki Jr. vs. Omar Ulises Huerta; 6 p.m. CT, April 11; ProBoxTV on YouTubeHarrison Campbell covers combat sports for The Tennessean and high school sports for The Daily Herald.
